    Protecting the Executive’s Privileges and Enhancing Efficiencies in Federal Contracting (opens in a new tab)
    PRESACT · web feed · White House Executive Orders · publisher-dated 2026-11-20 · corroborated: also received via web feed

    FAPD-AI: Executive Order 14438, titled "PROTECTING THE EXECUTIVE'S PRIVILEGES AND ENHANCING EFFICIENCIES IN FEDERAL CONTRACTING," dated November 20, 2026, requires all Federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and contracting agencies of pending or future congressional requests concerning their communications or work with the executive branch, and to follow instructions on withholding communications determined to be protected by executive privilege. The order directs the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance on compliance and provides that agencies shall consider contract termination or cancellation and contractor debarment or suspension for noncompliance. It also includes severability and general provisions, states that it creates no enforceable rights, and specifies that publication costs are borne by the Department of Labor. PRESACT-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:47:19 Eastern time ET
    National Adoption Month, 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    PRESACT · web feed · White House Presidential Actions · publisher-dated 2026-11-20

    FAPD-AI: The proclamation titled "NATIONAL ADOPTION MONTH, 2026," dated November 20, 2026, designates November 2026 as National Adoption Month and calls on Americans to ensure that every child has the love and support needed to live a long, healthy, and prosperous life. It references the expanded Adoption Tax Credit, the Fostering the Future Executive Order, the launch of Fostering the Future Accounts, and the FosteringTheFuture.gov website for youth transitioning from foster care. It also encourages faith-based organizations, houses of worship, businesses, nonprofits, and community groups to support adoptive families. PRESACT-SEL-02

    Byer v. Secretary of Health and Human Services (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cofc-1_24-vv-01595 / USCOURTS-cofc-1_24-vv-01595-0

    FAPD-AI: In Byer v. Secretary of Health and Human Services, No. 24-1595V, Special Master Nora Beth Dorsey issued a decision based on stipulation under the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program concerning a petition alleging Guillain-Barré syndrome from an influenza vaccine administered October 13, 2021. The parties' stipulation, filed October 20, 2026, provides a lump sum of $137,911.08 paid by ACH deposit to petitioner's counsel's IOLTA account, and the respondent denies that the vaccine caused the alleged injury. The special master adopted the stipulation as the decision of the court and directed the Clerk of Court to enter judgment absent a motion for review. USCOURTS-SEL-02

  • Observed at 21:27:23 Eastern time ET
    Branning v. Secretary of Health and Human Services (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cofc-1_25-vv-01788 / USCOURTS-cofc-1_25-vv-01788-0

    FAPD-AI: In Branning v. Secretary of Health and Human Services, No. 25-1788V, Chief Special Master Corcoran issued findings of fact and conclusions of law on October 14, 2026, dismissing the Table shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (SIRVA) claim. The special master found that the petitioner had not established by a preponderance of the evidence that her shoulder pain began within 48 hours of a September 24, 2024 influenza vaccination, relying on contemporaneous records placing onset three to four days after vaccination. The ruling states that an off-Table brachial neuritis claim remains viable and will be transferred out of the Special Processing Unit for resolution. USCOURTS-SEL-02

    USA v. Justin Bobo (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-26-05145 / USCOURTS-ca6-26-05145-0

    FAPD-AI: In a published opinion filed November 19, 2026, the Sixth Circuit affirmed a 194-month sentence imposed on Justin Bobo under the Armed Career Criminal Act after he pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The court held that Tennessee robbery remains categorically a violent felony under the ACCA, following its prior decision in United States v. Mitchell, because the Tennessee Supreme Court's decision in State v. Curry addressed only the crime-of-violence element of the unlawful possession statute and did not alter the fear element of robbery defined in State v. Taylor. Accordingly, Bobo's 2010 robbery conviction was held to qualify as a predicate violent felony. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:23:29 Eastern time ET
    United States v. Dedric Broyles (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca8-26-01670 / USCOURTS-ca8-26-01670-0

    FAPD-AI: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 19, 2026, the Eighth Circuit affirmed a 120-month sentence imposed on Dedric Dewayne Broyles for possession of a firearm by a felon following remand for resentencing. Counsel filed an Anders brief raising two potential issues: whether the district court made the sentence consecutive to an unrelated state-court sentence, and whether the written judgment added a supervised release condition. The court found no abuse of discretion in the consecutive sentence determination, concluded that the written judgment clarified an imprecisely pronounced condition, found no other non-frivolous issues, and granted counsel permission to withdraw. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:23:28 Eastern time ET
    International Construction Products LLC v. Caterpillar Inc. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-01635 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-01635-0

    FAPD-AI: This filing is the same nonprecedential opinion in International Construction Products, LLC v. Caterpillar Inc., issued under No. 25-1635, which is ICP's appeal (filed Nov. 19, 2026). The Third Circuit affirmed the District of Delaware's rulings on the cross-appeals, including the holding that ICP waived its North Carolina choice-of-law argument by litigating under Illinois law. The opinion also held that sufficient circumstantial evidence supported the jury's tortious interference finding and rejected Caterpillar's shareholder-interest privilege argument, and its discussion of the vacated $100 million damages award is truncated in the source. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:23:28 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Yanthonic Herrera (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-03145 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-03145-0

    FAPD-AI: In United States v. Yanthonic Herrera (3d Cir. No. 25-3145, filed Nov. 19, 2026), a nonprecedential opinion affirmed Herrera's conviction for possession with intent to distribute heroin and fentanyl, aiding and abetting, and his 300-month sentence. The court held that the warrant affidavit for Apartment 7131 established probable cause under the inference that drug dealers reside where they keep evidence, and that the Ker–Frisbie doctrine did not bar trial because no treaty specifically prohibiting abduction was identified. The opinion also addresses the Guidelines enhancements Herrera challenged, and that discussion is truncated in the source. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:23:28 Eastern time ET
    Marc Stephens v. CareOne Management LLC, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-03168 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-03168-0

    FAPD-AI: In Marc Stephens v. CareOne Management, LLC (3d Cir. No. 25-3168, filed Nov. 19, 2026), a per curiam nonprecedential opinion affirmed District of New Jersey orders in a pro se action asserting federal and state claims. The court held that CareOne and its employee were not state actors for purposes of 42 U.S.C. § 1983, that the complaint did not plausibly state a due process claim against the Englewood Defendants, and that a warrantless entry into the home following a 911 call was justified under the emergency aid exception. The court also held that the District Court did not abuse its discretion in declining supplemental jurisdiction over the state-law claims, and that Stephens forfeited his challenges to the magistrate judge's orders. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 21:23:28 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Oladapo Ogunbiyi (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-03300 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-03300-0

    FAPD-AI: In United States v. Oladapo Sunday Ogunbiyi (3d Cir. No. 25-3300, filed Nov. 19, 2026), a nonprecedential opinion affirmed a 41-month sentence entered by the District of New Jersey after a jury convicted Ogunbiyi of money laundering conspiracy, money laundering, and monetary transaction offenses. The court held that the two-level enhancement for sophisticated laundering under U.S.S.G. § 2S1.1(b)(3) applied, because the scheme used a fictitious entity, a shell corporation, and layered inter-account transfers. The court further held that Application Note 5(B) did not preclude the enhancement, because Ogunbiyi was not convicted of an offense underlying the money laundering charges. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Enacted law · govinfo API · PLAW-119publ29

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119–29, cited as the Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act, was approved July 24, 2025. It amends section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to let the Secretary of the Treasury, after consulting the FEMA Administrator and on written request of a State Governor (or the Mayor of the District of Columbia), apply deadline postponement rules to a qualified State-declared disaster, and it defines that term. It also extends the postponement period in that section from 60 days to 120 days, effective for declarations made after the date of enactment. PLAW-SEL-01

    Public Law 119–72: To amend title 38, United States Code, to modify the conditions under which the Secretary of Veteran… (opens in a new tab)
    Enacted law · govinfo API · PLAW-119publ72

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119–72, cited as the FAST VETS Act, was approved January 20, 2026. It amends section 3107(b) of title 38, United States Code, to set conditions under which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs reviews an individualized vocational rehabilitation plan. Under the amended provision, the Secretary may redevelop the plan with a veteran if the long-range rehabilitation goals are no longer feasible due to changes in the veteran's employment handicap and are likelier under a different plan, or may disapprove redevelopment if the Secretary determines it is not appropriate. PLAW-SEL-01

    Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act (opens in a new tab)
    Congressional Record · govinfo API · CREC-2026-11-19 / CREC-2026-11-19-pt1-PgS5788

    FAPD-AI: The Senate discharged the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee from H.R. 1520 and passed the bill, as amended by Senator Moody's substitute amendment (No. 7028), under the title 'Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act.' The bill prohibits covered entities from denying organ transplants or related services on the basis of disability and amends section 372(b)(2)(B) of the Public Health Service Act to bar disability-based medical criteria for organ allocation. The bill includes an exception that permits covered entities to consider disability following an individualized assessment in certain circumstances. Senator Moody requested unanimous consent for passage, and Senator Hassan spoke in support. CREC-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Senator Gillibrand, for Senator Cruz and Senator Rosen, proposed amendment SA 7029 to H.R. 4624, which would strike all after the enacting clause and insert the Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act of 2026. The amendment amends the Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996 to define unified boxing organizations and adds section 21A, which sets requirements including supplemental physical examinations for boxers aged 40 or older, additional ambulances and ringside physicians at covered matches, support services for contracted boxers, and a comprehensive anti-doping program. The amendment also provides for imprisonment of up to one year, a fine of up to $100,000, or both, for officers or employees who knowingly violate section 21A, with the fine increased for matches whose gross revenues exceed $2,000,000.     HR 5254 ENR: Gateway Partnership Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr5254enr

    FAPD-AI: H.R. 5254, the Gateway Partnership Act, is an enrolled bill from the second session of the 119th Congress that authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into a one-time agreement of up to five years with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to host private events at Gateway Arch National Park, including use of Park buildings. The agreement must include terms covering exclusive event dates, a monthly event maximum, National Park Service staffing levels, liability insurance naming the United States as additional insured, a federal liability exemption, and fees and cost recovery for maintenance, wear and tear, and other expenses. The authority sunsets seven years after enactment, and the Secretary must report to the House Committee on Natural Resources and the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources within four years on the agreement's operational and financial effects.     HR 8454 ENR: To provide for the transfer of administrative jurisdiction over certain Federal land in the State of Calif… (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr8454enr

    FAPD-AI: H.R. 8454 is an enrolled bill from the second session of the 119th Congress that transfers administrative jurisdiction over approximately 160 acres of National Forest System land in Tuolumne County, California, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior, to be managed as part of Yosemite National Park. It also transfers approximately 170 acres of National Park System land in the same county from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of Agriculture, to be managed as part of Stanislaus National Forest, with both transfers referencing the Ackerson Meadow Land Interchange map dated February 24, 2022. The bill permits the two Secretaries, by mutual agreement, to make minor survey and boundary corrections effective upon Federal Register publication, and it preserves valid existing rights and existing withdrawals, rights-of-way, easements, leases, licenses, and permits, which the receiving agency administers under applicable law.     Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-11-20 / 2026-23679

    official summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, and EC635T2+ helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of a separated tail rotor blade (TRB) assembly due to a crack caused by intergranular corrosion. This AD requires repetitively inspecting a certain TRB assembly for cracks and, depending on the results, removing any cracked TRB assembly from service and replacing an affected part as terminating action for the repetitive inspections. This AD also prohibits installing a certain TRB assembly on any helicopter unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt ( Taricha granulosa mazamae ), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish ( Cyprinodon tularosa ), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish. FR-SEL-02
